title: Auto Loans: Applicant and Amount Limits by Loan Product
content:
This card sets out, for every Auto Loans product offered by Piedmont Crescent Bank, the applicant age floor, the per-product holding limit and the band of amounts the bank will finance.

## What each column means

- **Minimum applicant age**: the applicant's age at the time of application, counted in whole years, may not be lower than this figure.
- **Loans of this product per customer**: the greatest number of loans of that same product, counting only loans that are applied for, active or delinquent, that one customer may have at once.
- **Smallest and largest amount financed**: the permitted range of the amount financed, in US dollars.
- **Loan-to-value ceiling**: the amount financed may reach at most this percentage of the vehicle's value, where the value is whichever is lower of the purchase price and the book value.

## Figures by product

| Loan product | Minimum applicant age (years) | Loans of this product per customer | Smallest amount financed (USD) | Largest amount financed (USD) | Loan-to-value ceiling (percent) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Used Vehicle Loan | 18 | 2 | 5000.00 | 75000.00 | 110 |
| Certified Pre-Owned Vehicle Loan | 18 | 2 | 7500.00 | 90000.00 | 120 |
| Auto Refinance Loan | 18 | 2 | 7500.00 | 90000.00 | 110 |
| Lease Buyout Loan | 18 | 1 | 10000.00 | 90000.00 | 110 |
| New Vehicle Loan | 18 | 2 | 7500.00 | 125000.00 | 125 |
| Green Vehicle Loan | 18 | 2 | 7500.00 | 125000.00 | 125 |

## Points of judgement

**Which value does the loan-to-value ceiling use?** The lower of two figures: the price paid for the vehicle and its book value. A high purchase price never lifts the ceiling above what the book value supports, and the reverse is equally true.

**Is the holding limit shared across products?** The column above counts loans of one product only. The Lease Buyout Loan is the one product where a customer may hold a single loan at a time; every other product allows two.

## Illustration (hypothetical figures)

Suppose a vehicle is bought for 30000.00 dollars and carries a book value of 28000.00 dollars, financed as a Used Vehicle Loan. The value used is 28000.00, the lower of the two. A ceiling of 110 percent of that value gives 30800.00 dollars as the most that may be financed against this vehicle. The purchase price and book value here are invented for the example and describe no real customer.
